clue.text: Note for musician's apartment

definitions.meaning: a pitch a semitone below the note A in the scale
read as a phrase, one set of rooms where a musician might live

explanation.surface: A message left for someone about a musician's lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'for' is only a link between the two readings: one musical, one domestic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the same letters: a pitch name with a flat sign, and a set of rooms on one floor.

clue.text: Queen Anne's Scottish doctor who sermonized supporting the union (a "no voter?)

definitions.text: Queen Anne's Scottish doctor who sermonized supporting the union (a "no voter?)

parts.words: Queen Anne's Scottish doctor who sermonized supporting the union (a "no voter?)
parts.note: the royal physician and satirist, creator of John Bull, who wrote in favour of the 1707 Union, likened to a 'No' voter in the 2014 Scottish referendum

explanation.surface: A Scottish court physician preaching for the union, imagined as a modern 'No' campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 2014 Scottish independence referendum a 'No' vote was a vote to keep the union with England, which this eighteenth-century Scot also championed.
explanation.definitionFit: John, the Scottish satirist, was physician to Queen Anne and a pamphleteer for the Anglo-Scottish union.

clue.text: Organist at St Mark's, Venice, shows sales item by returning it

parts.note: a lot is an item put up at an auction sale

indicators.note: the word it is turned round and set by the first piece

explanation.surface: A Venetian church organist is caught selling something and then giving it back.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio, the Baroque composer, served as first organist at the basilica of San Marco in Venice.

clue.text: "How from this —, hopes which dive, / And fears which soar" (Browning, 1883)

definitions.text: "How from this —, hopes which dive, / And fears which soar" (Browning, 1883)

parts.words: "How from this —, hopes which dive, / And fears which soar" (Browning, 1883)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Browning's Ferishtah's Fancies, the gap a Hebrew-derived word for chaos

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian verse with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is a term for utter confusion or chaos, matching the tumbling hopes and fears of the lines.

clue.text: Woman in holy orders, much seen at raves

definitions.text: Woman in holy orders, much seen at raves

parts.words: Woman in holy orders, much seen at raves
parts.note: a priestess of the wine god, whose rites were wild revels, here dressed up as a modern partygoer

explanation.surface: A nun who turns up at a lot of all-night dance parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy orders' suggests a nun, but the religion is the ancient cult of Bacchus, and 'raves' are its frenzied rites.
explanation.definitionFit: A female devotee or priestess of Bacchus took part in drunken orgiastic revels.

clue.text: Shakespeare not wanted here, they say

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: someone not wanted is barred from a place

explanation.surface: Shakespeare is unwelcome in some place, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright is traditionally called the Bard of Avon, a bard being a poet.

clue.text: Prisoner with false coin takes a month to produce this cobbled fiction

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: takes means one piece holds another within it
false here says the letters of coin are not genuine, so rearrange them

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October, a month

explanation.surface: A convict forges a coin over a month and comes up with a tall story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' makes the anagram CION, and 'takes' has it hold the month's abbreviation just after its first letter; 'this cobbled fiction' defines the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A concoction is something invented or made up, like a hastily assembled story.

clue.text: Northern novelist in wood close at hand

parts.note: a holt is an old word for a wood or copse
by means near, as in 'stand by'

explanation.surface: A writer from the north is in a forest near by.
explanation.walkthrough: Winifred, author of South Riding, was a Yorkshire novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Winifred was a novelist from Yorkshire in the north of England.

clue.text: Believer in heresy of old soldier -a Scot?

parts.note: Nestor is the aged warrior-king in Homer's Iliad
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A Scottish veteran is accused of holding heretical beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Nestorius held the condemned doctrine that Christ's divine and human natures were separate persons.

clue.text: First Emily Bronte offering — all right to provide computer reading

indicators.note: first applies to each of the three words after it, taking its opening letter

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: Emily Bronte's debut novel is fine for reading on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital book is read on a computer or tablet rather than on paper.

clue.text: Where the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, reports The Book of the Just Man

definitions.text: Where the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, reports The Book of the Just Man

parts.words: Where the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, reports The Book of the Just Man
parts.note: Joshua 10 cites the Book of Jasher (the upright) for the day the sun halted over Gibeon during the pursuit down a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A biblical miracle site, according to an ancient lost book.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshua chased the Amorites down the ascent of this town on the day the sun and moon stood still.

clue.text: "Before it could recover Garcia's — whizzed through the air and lighted on its neck" (Beerbohm, Wanderings in Patagonia)

definitions.text: "Before it could recover Garcia's — whizzed through the air and lighted on its neck" (Beerbohm, Wanderings in Patagonia)

parts.words: "Before it could recover Garcia's — whizzed through the air and lighted on its neck" (Beerbohm, Wanderings in Patagonia)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation: the missing item is a cowboy's noosed rope thrown to catch an animal

explanation.surface: A gaucho's throw in a Patagonian travel book, with one word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A noosed rope thrown through the air to catch cattle or horses fits the scene.

clue.text: Du Maurier work now seen as old hat

definitions.meaning: George du Maurier's 1894 novel about an artist's model and Svengali
a soft felt hat with an indented crown, old-fashioned now

explanation.surface: A Du Maurier book is now considered passe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like the idiom for out of date; it is literally an old-style hat, named after the novel's heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel gave its name to the narrow-brimmed felt headwear worn in its stage version.

clue.text: He realises Tony in Mark Twain tonight

definitions.text: He realises Tony in Mark Twain tonight

parts.words: He realises Tony in Mark Twain tonight
parts.note: the American actor won a Tony award for his one-man show Mark Twain Tonight!

explanation.surface: An actor brings the author to life on stage and wins a theatre award.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tony is the top American theatre award; 'realises' means both brings to life and achieves.
explanation.definitionFit: Hal, the US actor, won the 1966 Tony for impersonating the humorist in a solo show.

clue.text: Oxford college writer from Ireland

definitions.meaning: a women's college founded at Oxford in 1879
Edith, co-author with Martin Ross of the Irish R.M. stories

explanation.surface: An Irish author attended a college in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is shared by an Oxford college and by Edith, the Anglo-Irish novelist.

clue.text: Elizabeth Gaskell's poles apart seen together

definitions.text: Elizabeth Gaskell's poles apart seen together

parts.words: Elizabeth Gaskell's poles apart seen together
parts.note: Gaskell's novel title names two opposite compass points; join them with a hyphen instead of 'and'

explanation.surface: Gaskell's novel about two regions that are worlds apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite compass points of Gaskell's 1855 novel are 'poles apart', and dropping her 'and' sees them together.
explanation.definitionFit: Two opposed compass directions joined make a single hyphenated term for an axis.

clue.text: Again fill pen with relish, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters offered could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Refill a pen and enjoy doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill something up again, as with ink or supplies, is the sense.

clue.text: Longer version of Aiken's child becomes piratical

definitions.text: Longer version of Aiken's child becomes piratical

parts.words: Longer version of Aiken's child becomes piratical
parts.note: Joan Aiken's word for a child, given one more letter, becomes the name of a famous Scottish privateer

explanation.surface: In a children's author's story, a youngster grows up to be a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain William was hanged in 1701 for piracy.

clue.text: Philosophical interpreter of the Tarot de Marseille?

definitions.text: Philosophical interpreter of the Tarot de Marseille?

parts.words: Philosophical interpreter of the Tarot de Marseille?
parts.note: the French philosopher's surname read as French 'of the cards', fit for a tarot reader

explanation.surface: A thinker who reads fortunes from a French tarot pack.
explanation.walkthrough: The French tarot pack suggests a fortune-teller; the philosopher's name, split, is French for 'of the cards'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rene, author of 'I think, therefore I am', is the philosopher whose name splits into French for 'of the cards'.

clue.text: Anatolian men of steel may offer Bach's Ely

indicators.note: may offer says the letters could be presented in a different order

parts.note: the composer's name with its possessive s, all letters used

explanation.surface: A Bach piece played at Ely Cathedral might yield ironworkers of old Asia Minor.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient people of the Black Sea coast of Anatolia were renowned ironworkers; Greek 'chalyps' means steel.

clue.text: Kind to lead writer and cast

definitions.text: Kind to lead writer and cast

parts.words: Kind to lead writer and cast
parts.note: a word for a kind which, put in front, makes a machine for writing and a verb for stereotyping actors

explanation.surface: A director is gentle with the leading writer and actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective (generous), but it is a noun: sort or class.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort or class, which also prefixes 'writer' and 'cast'.

clue.text: Philosopher discredited one NHS apex

indicators.note: discredited suggests a reputation, here the letters, being knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A thinker has undermined the head of the health service.
explanation.walkthrough: NHS is Britain's National Health Service; 'discredited' rearranges ONE, NHS and APEX.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek of Colophon was a pre-Socratic thinker and poet who mocked the gods of Homer.

clue.text: Investigating Inspector encountered in Passage to the North

parts.note: an alley is a narrow passage between buildings
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A detective is met in a northern alleyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderick is Ngaio Marsh's detective inspector of Scotland Yard.

clue.text: Schiller had a hand in it

definitions.text: Schiller had a hand in it

parts.words: Schiller had a hand in it
parts.note: Schiller's ballad Der Handschuh, translated, names an item worn on the hand

explanation.surface: Schiller was involved in some scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a hand in it' is the idiom for being involved; literally a hand goes inside the item, the title of his ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: Schiller's ballad tells of a knight sent into a lion pit to retrieve a lady's dropped handwear.

clue.text: Son of Apollo, easily becoming tense, killed in Trojan War

definitions.text: Son of Apollo, easily becoming tense, killed in Trojan War

parts.words: Son of Apollo, easily becoming tense, killed in Trojan War
parts.note: a hero slain by Achilles on his island, whose name rearranges at once into a word meaning taut

explanation.surface: A god's anxious son died in the Trojan conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Tenedos, said to be a son of Apollo, was killed by Achilles on the way to Troy.

clue.text: De Goncourt's professional girl carries an aspirate for prophet

parts.note: Edmond de Goncourt's novel La Fille Elisa is about a prostitute named Elisa
the letter H is the aspirate, the breathed sound

explanation.surface: A French novelist's working girl breathes out a prophet's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts H inside ELISA, after its S.

clue.text: French author in long narrative (new)

parts.note: a saga is a long story

explanation.surface: A French writer features in a lengthy new tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Francoise wrote Bonjour Tristesse; she is a French novelist.

clue.text: Clasped by Tennyson's eagle

parts.note: Tennyson's poem The Eagle begins 'He clasps' this rocky height 'with crooked hands'

explanation.surface: Something gripped in the talons of a bird in a Tennyson poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep rugged rock face is what the bird grips at the opening of the poem.

clue.text: Sound from piano is exceptional

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The tone of a piano is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a musical tone; it is the definition, and the letters run through 'piano is exceptional'.
explanation.definitionFit: A din or any audible sound fits the sense.

clue.text: Nobleman acquired by British Isles to take a part in King John

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman
BI is the abbreviation for British Isles
got means acquired

explanation.surface: An aristocrat gained by Britain is cast in a Shakespeare history play.
explanation.definitionFit: This English earl is one of the roles in Shakespeare's history play of King John.

clue.text: Composer from beautiful mountain in Germany

parts.note: German schon means beautiful, the clue's 'in Germany' asking for German
German Berg means mountain

explanation.surface: A composer from a lovely German peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Germany' asks for both pieces in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold, the Austrian, pioneered twelve-tone music in the twentieth century.

clue.text: Some of Blake's are more sophisticated than others

definitions.text: Some of Blake's are more sophisticated than others

parts.words: Some of Blake's are more sophisticated than others
parts.note: Blake published poems 'of Innocence' and 'of Experience', the second set the worldlier

explanation.surface: A comment that some Blake works are more refined than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more sophisticated' points to Experience as against Innocence in Blake's paired collections.
